articles.headline: ARCA Menards Series Pre-Season Rankings Place Jake Bollman at the Top
articles.dek: The Arca Menards field looks toward the opening green flag with Nitro Motorsports locking down the top three spots in the power rankings.
articles.body:
The voters has spoken before a single competitive lap is turned in the ARCA Menards Series. Officials released the pre-season power rankings on February 12, 2026, setting the baseline for the upcoming twenty-race calendar. Jake Bollman leads the initial list with a power score of 89, heading a formidable trio at the top of the board.

Bollman shares the penthouse view of the garage with teammates Nicholas Hoggeton and Samuel Riggs, who also secured an 89 power score to sweep the top three positions for their shop. The opening image from the league office highlights the tight grouping at the summit before the rest of the garage fills in the remaining slots down to James Baker rounding out the top ten at 48.

Mid-pack positions feature Alfie Denley, Atsz Minyoung, and Bryce Applegate all holding a 40 power score. Caleb Guerrier, Daniel Dominguez, and Eric Caudell occupy the subsequent spots on the league table as teams finalize setups for the season opener. With no races in the books yet, these figures reflect off-season simulator data and equipment evaluations rather than hard race results.

Attention now shifts to the official start of the schedule. Teams must back up their pre-season status when the green flag waves for the first time.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Contract Year Pressure Mounts for Bollman and Newman
articles.dek: Drivers entering the final year of their current deals look to secure their futures early.
articles.body:
The start of a new racing season brings added pressure for competitors navigating the final year of their current agreements. Squad evaluations are already underway behind the scenes as garage personnel look ahead to future roster stability.

Jake Bollman enters the 2026 campaign at Nitro Motorsports on an expiring deal. Bollman showed encouraging pace during the recent Daytona test by placing sixth overall, providing a positive foundation as contract discussions loom in the coming months.

Kolby Newman faces a similar situation at Maples Motorsports. Newman logged a lap of 48.081 seconds during the January test session and aims to establish early consistency to solidify his standing within the organization.

Team directors maintain that early-season performance dictates the timeline for negotiations. While no formal announcements are expected immediately, strong finishes in the opening rounds at superspeedways and short tracks traditionally accelerate talks between drivers and management.
articles.author: Cole Whitaker

pullQuote.text: Early-season performance dictates the timeline for negotiations.

takeaways: Contract year pressure affects multiple drivers.
Team evaluations begin during pre-season testing.
extras.whatsNext: Track action begins at Daytona with the General Tire 200.

articles.headline: Daytona Open Test Concludes Ahead of General Tire 200
articles.dek: Teams wrap up pre-race preparations following a busy day of drafting practice at Daytona.
articles.body:
Track activity has concluded for the ARCA Menards Series preseason test at Daytona International Speedway. Competitors used the sessions to evaluate aerodynamic setups and engine durability in drafting packs ahead of the February 14 season opener.

Jade Avedisian led the final speed chart for Nitro Motorsports with a lap of 46.610 seconds. Andy Jankowiak finished second fastest for KLAS Motorsports at 46.613 seconds, followed by Willie Mullins in third with a time of 46.756 seconds.

McCoy Behnke placed fourth for SPS Racing at 46.805 seconds, and Alfie Denley rounded out the top five for CR7 Motorsports at 46.829 seconds. Twenty drivers recorded official lap times during the test session.

Teams will now spend the intervening weeks fine-tuning chassis setups and completing final sponsor obligations before official practice begins for the General Tire 200.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

pullQuote.text: Teams used the sessions to evaluate aerodynamic setups.

takeaways: Testing focused heavily on drafting configurations.
No major incidents were reported during the sessions.
extras.whatsNext: Opening practice for the General Tire 200 gets underway race week.

articles.headline: Preseason Form Guide Points Toward Nitro Motorsports at Daytona
articles.dek: A comprehensive look at the field reveals clear favorites as the ARCA Menards Series prepares for Daytona.
articles.body:
The open test at Daytona International Speedway provided the first real look at the 2026 ARCA Menards Series grid. While teams traditionally hide their true speed during testing, the time sheets offer valuable clues about who holds early momentum heading into the General Tire 200.

Jade Avedisian set the pace in the opening test session, touring the 2.5-mile superspeedway in 46.610 seconds behind the wheel of the number 15 entry for Nitro Motorsports. Teammate Jake Bollman also showed strong pace, posting the sixth-fastest lap at 46.906 seconds. Samuel Riggs rounds out the Nitro stable, establishing a solid baseline during the January sessions.

KLAS Motorsports figures to be a primary challenger right away. Andy Jankowiaks posted the second-quickest time of the test at 46.613 seconds, missing the top spot by just three thousandths of a second in the number 71 machine.

Joe Gibbs Racing enters the season with high expectations, placing Max Reaves ninth in test speeds with a 47.126 lap. Pinnacle Racing Group brings a pair of capable drivers in Valdemar Estriden and Nick Apollo, who managed eighth and fifteenth respectively during the open test.

Mid-tier operations and independent entries continue to sort out their programs. Willie Mullins extracted significant speed from his number 3 car to claim third overall, while McCoy Behnke put SPS Racing fourth on the chart. The General Tire 200 will ultimately test race setups rather than single-lap speed, making drafting and track position paramount when the green flag waves.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

pullQuote.text: The open test at Daytona provided the first real look at the grid.

takeaways: Nitro Motorsports showed speed across multiple entries.
KLAS Motorsports is immediately competitive at the top.
Testing speeds rarely reflect full race runs.
extras.whatsNext: The field returns to Daytona International Speedway for the season-opening General Tire 200.

articles.headline: James Baker out just as quickly as he came in>
articles.dek: Fresh chatter in the ARCA Menards Series garage suggests top prospect James Baker could be eyeing a fast-tracked move to the Truck Series as early as next year.
articles.body:
Industry insiders are openly discussing the trajectory of prospect James Baker, with paddock whispers indicating an early exit from the ARCA ranks could happen as soon as next season.

While the 2026 season has yet to officially get underway, team evaluators are already weighing the long-term value of keeping top-tier talent in developmental divisions. Baker has drawn consistent attention from scouts tracking simulated lower-tier series. A potential leap to national touring series trucks would reshape the driver market significantly.

For now, teams remain focused on the immediate 20-race ARCA schedule ahead. Preseason preparations continue across the board, but the looming prospect of a departure adds an intriguing subplot to the garage area before a single lap has been turned.

Observers note that early promotion talks are rare this far in advance of the season opener. Whether these rumors materialize into concrete garage movement remains to be seen once the racing actually gets underway.
articles.author: Cole Whitaker

john verstappen.name: John Verstappen
john verstappen.bio: John Verstappen grew up working on dairy equipment in rural Wisconsin before helping his uncle prep street stocks at the local half-mile oval. He spent seven years running regional touring divisions, slowly building a reputation as a clean, low-maintenance driver who rarely tore up equipment. Now piloting the 98 for Shearer Speed Racing, he approaches race weekends with a quiet, blue-collar work ethic.

james baker.name: James Baker
james baker.bio: Raised just blocks away from several race shops, James Baker spent his childhood shagging tires and sweeping floors for local mechanics. He climbed through the legends car ranks and lower-tier regional series by securing small-business backing from industrial suppliers in the Piedmont region. Today, he handles the pressure of the 18 car at Joe Gibbs Racing with an analytical, reserved demeanor.

vincent crook.name: Vincent Crook
vincent crook.bio: Vincent Crook started racing go-karts on temporary asphalt setups in Pacific Northwest industrial parks. After years of self-funding his late model efforts through a commercial plumbing business, he finally caught a break in regional stock car touring series. He brings a gritty, pragmatic approach to the 89 entry for Rise Racing with Earnhardt-Shearer Racing.

kolby newman.name: Kolby Newman
kolby newman.bio: Kolby Newman spent his teens racing dirt modifieds across the Midwest circuits with his father acting as crew chief and engine builder. He transitioned to asphalt via regional developmental combines, showing steady car control on intermediate tracks. Now driving the 99 for Maples Motorsports, he is still learning how to manage full-distance race strategies.

caleb guerrier.name: Caleb Guerrier
caleb guerrier.bio: Caleb Guerrier grew up around swamp buggy races before pivoting to asphalt street stock racing in his early twenties. He bounced through various underfunded independent teams for over a decade, keeping rides afloat with sheer mechanical persistence. Currently piloting the 06 for Wayne Peterson Motorsports, he acts as an on-track veteran who keeps expectations grounded.

nick apollo.name: Nick Apollo
nick apollo.bio: Nick Apollo worked on his family's construction fleet before finding a seat in northeastern modified tour races. He ground out a living racing weekly shows for spare parts money before earning a spot in developmental stock car series. Driving the 77 for Pinnacle Racing Group, he relies on a defensive driving style honed on tight, abrasive short tracks.

samuel riggs.name: Samuel Riggs
samuel riggs.bio: Samuel Riggs learned vehicle dynamics by maintaining heavy machinery on his family's Panhandle cattle ranch. He transitioned to local asphalt late models after winning a regional factory-backed driver search. Now behind the wheel of the 55 for Nitro Motorsports, he is known for a calm disposition inside a racecar regardless of handling issues.

nicholas hoggeton.name: Nicholas Hoggeton
nicholas hoggeton.bio: Nicholas Hoggeton grew up attending weekly races at local Virginia short tracks with his grandfather. He worked his way through the regional truck and late model divisions by trading mechanical labor for seat time. In the 70 car for Nitro Motorsports, he remains a straightforward competitor who focuses on preserving equipment for the final stage.

tyler payne.name: Tyler Payne
tyler payne.bio: Tyler Payne started in Midwest quarter midgets before moving up through regional asphalt stock car series. He balanced college classes in mechanical engineering with weekend travel to various short tracks across the Great Lakes. Piloting the 79 for ACR Motorsports, he approaches car setups with a technical mindset and calculated execution.

william faison.name: William Faison
william faison.bio: William Faison spent his early years working in coastal boatyards before funding his own hobby stock racing hobby. He spent over a decade quietly climbing the regional ladder without the benefit of major sponsorship backing. Driving the 86 for Clubb Racing Inc., he relies on his extensive endurance racing background to manage worn-out tires.

daniel dominguez.name: Daniel Dominguez
daniel dominguez.bio: Daniel Dominguez started racing in desert off-road events before shifting to regional pavement late models in the Southwest. He has spent the last fifteen years serving as a journeyman driver for various low-budget operations. In the 48 for Brad Smith Motorsports, he provides steady experience and honest feedback to the crew.

daniel stavchanksy.name: Daniel Stavchanksy
daniel stavchanksy.bio: Daniel Stavchanksy grew up racing local asphalt legends cars while studying industrial fabrication. He progressed through regional developmental series by securing localized backing from heavy manufacturing firms. Now driving the 03 for Clubb Racing Inc., he brings a methodical and cautious approach to every race.

alfie denley.name: Alfie Denley
alfie denley.bio: Alfie Denley spent his adolescence racing outlaw karts on bullrings across the Pacific Northwest. He moved south to the Carolinas as a teenager to pursue pavement racing opportunities in lower-tier touring divisions. Piloting the 97 for CR7 Motorsports, he is working to adapt his aggressive dirt instincts to heavy stock cars on paved tracks.

atsz minyoung.name: Atsz Minyoung
atsz minyoung.bio: Atsz Minyoung started driving ice-races on frozen lakes before relocating to the lower forty-eight to pursue pavement stock car racing. He worked as a fabricator for various regional teams while scraping together funds for occasional starts. Behind the wheel of the 12 for Fast Track Racing, he is recognized for car control in low-grip conditions.

valdemar estriden.name: Valdemar Estriden
valdemar estriden.bio: Valdemar Estriden grew up racing street stock cars on freezing northern bullrings during short summer seasons. He gradually worked his way up through regional touring series, maintaining his own cars out of a single-bay garage. Now driving the 28 for Pinnacle Racing Group, he is known for keeping a cool head under chaotic race conditions.

mccoy behnke.name: McCoy Behnke
mccoy behnke.bio: McCoy Behnke spent his youth wrenching on pickup trucks and racing local asphalt bombers in Big Sky country. He transitioned to regional touring series after winning a series of local short track championships. Driving the 24 for SPS Racing, he is a quiet competitor focused on bringing the car home in one piece.
